facts.raw_span: A 22-year-old woman
history of systemic lupus erythematosus
fever
Temperature of 101.5°F
Erythematous plaques with superficial desquamation in the malar distribution of the face, nose, ears, and medial forehead
Several large bullae on the right arm
Numerous flat and raised 2-zoned atypical targets with dusky centers on the forearms, abdomen, back, thighs, legs, palms and soles
Normocytic anemia (mean corpuscular volume: 99 fL; hemoglobin: 11.7 g/dL; hematocrit: 33.4%)
Platelet count: 81 K/μL (thrombocytopenia)
Antinuclear antibody titer: 1:1280 (speckled pattern)
Punch biopsy of abdominal target lesion showed dyskeratosis with superficial perivascular inflammation and interface changes
Dusky malar erythema with focal heme crusting

concepts.why: The patient has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus and presents with fever, erythematous plaques, and a high antinuclear antibody titer.
The patient presents with erythematous plaques and target lesions, consistent with acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus.
The patient has a low platelet count, which is a common finding in systemic lupus erythematosus.
The patient has a normocytic anemia, which is a common finding in systemic lupus erythematosus.
The patient presents with bullae and target lesions, consistent with bullous lupus erythematosus.
The patient has a high antinuclear antibody titer and presents with signs of kidney involvement, consistent with lupus nephritis.
